title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-breadcrumbs-6
content:
Timestamp: 2026-02-25 -> 2026-03-02
Owner: Marcus Chen (eng-serving-runtime)
Goal: capture breadcrumbs from recent Dedicated GPU pool autoscale incidents (capacity thrash + warmup delays). Raw notes, commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.

Context
- Multiple incidents in the last 2 weeks where Dedicated GPU pools went into capacity-thrash: rapid scale-up/scale-down cycles causing a flurry of cold starts and request failures. Symptoms: spike in 503/429s, long tail token latencies for affected customers, increased infra costs.
- Pattern: sudden traffic bumps (customer loadtests or real bursts) + provisioning delays + model warmup/cold-cache causing autoscaler to overshoot/undershoot.

Observed timeline (high level)
- 2026-02-18 11:12 UTC: Customer A ramped traffic (internal stress test). Pool A reported CPU pressure -> pods evicted -> autoscaler triggered node provisioning.
- 2026-02-18 11:18 UTC: New nodes registered but kube-scheduler places pods slowly due to image pulls and node GPU driver init. Pod ready time ~3-6m.
- 2026-02-18 11:24 UTC: Autoscaler sees pending pods -> adds more nodes -> repeated. By 11:35 we had 3 provisioning rounds.
- Consequence: many containers started before model weights fully warmed up -> requests hit cold processes -> long first-token latencies and queue buildup -> autoscaler interpreted high pending/latency as need for even more capacity -> capacity thrash.

Commands & logs (scrapbook)
- kubectl get nodes --selector=pool=dedicated-A -o wide  # node up/down timeline
- kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=dedicated-A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.phase} {.status.containerStatuses[*].ready} {.status.startTime}
'
- k get hpa -n serving dedicated-a-autoscaler -o yaml
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels:dedicated-a" --sort-by=~creationTimestamp

Example error snippets (copied)
- "pod "serve-abc-0" evicted: The node had condition: [MemoryPressure]."
- "Failed to pull image \"gcr.io/redwood/serve:prod-202602\": manifest unknown" (transient on one provisioning wave)
- "first-token-latency: 21.4s (cold)" (observed via per-request tracing)
- "503: backend_busy" (internal gateway returned while container warming)

Prom queries I used during incident
- rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",status=503}[5m])
- histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="serve",pool="dedicated-A"}[5m])) by (le))
- sum(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="serving",pool="dedicated-A"})

Things we tried / quick mitigations (notes)
- Increased minReplicaCount for high-SLA routes to 2 -> reduces cold starts but increases baseline cost.
- Temporarily bumped stabilizationWindow for the autoscaler to 180s to avoid rapid scaling in/out. Helped reduce thrash but led to under-provisioning for very large bursts.
- Pre-pulled images via DaemonSet on nodes (image pull warmup) -> shaved ~30s from pod ready time in a controlled test.
- Introduced a lightweight warmup probe: postStart exec that warms small shard of the model weights. Mixed results: some models crash on partial init.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Provisioning latency (cloud instance creation + GPU driver init + image download) is bigger than our autoscaler window -> autoscaler triggers multiple waves.
2) Model cold start (weights load + JIT/quant kernels) contributes >50% of pod ready latency; autoscaler metrics (pending pods / CPU pressure) don't capture model warmup state.
3) Some transient image registry failures (rare) cause pods to remain pending and amplify autoscaler decisions.
4) Cache/kv (prefix caching) misses on new pods create a request storm on model init causing backpressure and more pending requests.

Tests to validate hypotheses (short term)
- Measure full provisioning latency pipeline end-to-end: instance create -> kubelet ready -> image pulled -> nvidia driver ready -> container ready -> model ready (we currently log most but not aggregated). Build a single histogram metric "pool_provisioner_end_to_model_ready_seconds".
- Run controlled scale test with forced long model warmup (sleep in init) to see autoscaler behavior.
- Simulate registry pull failures in canary to see if autoscaler overreacts.

Potential fixes (brainstorm)
- Autoscaler changes:
  - Make autoscaler warmup-aware: use a custom readiness metric from pod that reports model-ready (boolean gauge). Scale decisions consider model-ready count not just pod ready.
  - Add cooldown/stabilization heuristics per pool: exponential backoff on scale-down when scale-up happened in last X minutes.
- Provisioning improvements:
  - Pre-warm images and drivers: have a pool of kept-warm nodes (standing warm capacity) that are always image+driver ready and can take traffic immediately.
  - Use faster instance types for initial warmup nodes (spot/ephemeral) then migrate workloads to reserved instances when stable.
- Model/runtime changes:
  - Split init: minimal runtime process that can accept light traffic (proxy) while heavy weights load async; route non-critical requests to proxy and heavy to warmed replicas.
  - Persist KV caches across pod restarts (shared cache) to avoid heavy recomputation on warmup.

Open action items (next steps)
- (Aisha) Instrument total provisioning->model-ready latency metric and add to dashboards (ENG-3421).
- (Ravi) Run a controlled warmup failure test in staging: simulate slow image pulls and slow model init; capture autoscaler decision logs.
- (Marcus) Prototype a model-ready pod readiness gauge (small sidecar that marks model_ready=1 when weights loaded) and test autoscaler logic in a canary pool.
- Draft proposal for a small always-warm capacity (cost estimate + risk) and share with infra leads by 2026-03-05.

Notes to self (informal)
- Watch the PR #558 for autoscaler changes; might need tweaks to kube-controller-manager flags.
- Keep customers informed: propose a postmortem blurb focusing on mitigations and timeline.

Raw command history (snippet)
- gcloud compute instances create-from-container warm-node-1 --container-image=gcr.io/redwood/serve:prod-202602 --labels=pool=dedicated-A --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1"
- kubectl apply -f warmup-patch.yaml -n serving
- curl -sS http://gateway.internal/health?route=customer-a | jq

End of breadcrumbs. Will iterate after we have the provisioning->model-ready histogram.

-- Marcus
